cards.text: This is Psalm 145, a psalm of praise from David, Israel's king. David's got the throne, the crown, the whole royal setup. And the first thing he does is talk straight to God and call Him 'my God and King.'

cards.question: King David has a King of his own. How long does David say he'll bless God's name?

answers.text: For the rest of his reign

cards.question: David plans to save his praise for the big days, like feasts and victories.

cards.text: Every day, not just the big ones. Then David turns from talking to God to talking about Him: "Great is the LORD and greatly to be praised; His greatness is unsearchable."

cards.question: David says the LORD's greatness is unsearchable. What does he mean?

answers.text: No one can ever reach the end of it
God keeps it hidden from His people
Only kings are able to understand it

cards.text: Friend, I lived in a junk drawer for YEARS and never found the bottom of that pile of old takeout menus. And that was a DRAWER.

cards.question: David looks way past his own lifetime. He pictures each ___ telling the next one about God's mighty acts.

cards.text: While the generations pass it down, David says he'll meditate on God's wondrous works. Not skim them like a group chat with 400 unread messages. MEDITATE.

cards.question: In these lines, David goes back and forth between what 'they' will proclaim and what 'I' will do.

cards.text: They'll celebrate the fame of God's abundant goodness and sing joyfully of His righteousness. Everybody's talking, everybody's singing, and it's all about ONE God.
Then David stops telling you who's talking about God. He tells you what God is actually like.

cards.question: David describes the LORD as quick to anger but just as quick to calm down.

cards.text: "The LORD is gracious and compassionate, slow to anger and abounding in loving devotion." That's close to how the LORD described Himself to Moses, way back in Exodus 34:6.

cards.question: David just said the LORD is gracious and compassionate. Who does he say the LORD is good to?

answers.text: Only the ones who praise Him

cards.text: Generations of people praising God. That's already a BIG crowd. Now David widens the circle even more.

cards.question: David says only people will give the LORD thanks, and the rest of what He made stays quiet.

cards.text: All He made gives Him thanks, and His saints bless Him. Then those saints open their mouths and tell of the glory of His kingdom and speak of His might.

cards.question: The saints talk about God's kingdom and His might. Why do they do it?

answers.text: So people would know His mighty acts
So their enemies would be afraid
So God would reward them for it

cards.text: Now remember who's talking here. A king, with his own throne, talking about Somebody else's kingdom.

cards.question: David says God's kingdom is an ___ kingdom, and His dominion endures through all generations.

cards.text: Friend, I got pulled out of a clearance bin for 25 cents when the bakery I came from closed for good. God's kingdom? NO closing day.

cards.question: David says the LORD is faithful in all His words, not just some of them.
David moves from God's kingdom to what this King does for people. What does the LORD do for all who fall or are bowed down?

answers.text: He holds them up and lifts them
He waits for them to stand alone
He sends someone else to help

cards.text: He lifts up ALL who are bowed down. Friend, I was bowed down in the back of a junk drawer so long the dust started charging me rent.
Then David pictures the eyes of all looking to the LORD. Like a kitchen full of bakers staring at the oven door, waiting on that timer.

cards.question: All eyes look to the LORD. What does He give them?

cards.text: "You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living thing." Friend, I've got a whole mustache for hands, and I can't satisfy ONE baker who wants extra sprinkles.

cards.question: David says the LORD is righteous in His ways, but only kind to the people who earn it.

cards.text: Then David takes on a question a lot of us carry around. How close is God, really?

cards.question: Who does David say the LORD is near to?

answers.text: All who call on Him in truth
Only the priests in the temple

cards.question: For those who fear the LORD, what does He do when they cry out?

answers.text: He hears them and saves them
He tests them a while longer
He tells them to wait quietly

cards.question: David draws a line between those who love the LORD and the wicked. He says the LORD preserves both groups.

cards.text: And David ends right where he started, with his own mouth declaring the praise of the LORD. 'Forever and ever' shows up again, just like in his first two lines.

cards.question: In his last line, David calls on every ___ to bless the LORD's holy name forever and ever.

findings.problem: The card opens with 'Every day, not just the big ones,' which retells Psalm 145:2. But the card cites only Psalm 145:3. It should cite Psalm 145:2-3.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the junk drawer. It tells no part of the passage and doesn't move the baker forward. It restates verse 3, which card 4 already told. The joke should ride along on a card that tells part of the psalm.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The answers aren't the same kind of thing. 'generation' and 'household' are groups of people, but 'priest' is one person.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: 'While the generations pass it down' says David's meditating happens at the same time as the generations' proclaiming. Verse 5 only says 'And I will meditate,' so the text leaves that connection open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'In these lines' points back to cards that are no longer on screen. The question never says which lines, or what 'they' proclaim and what David says 'I' will do.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' and the right answer is the one broad option, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: The blank comes right after 'an', so only a word that starts with a vowel sound fits. That rules out 'chosen' by grammar alone and points to the right answer.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: This story card is only a joke about the clearance bin. It tells no new part of the passage. It restates the everlasting kingdom from card 6 and doesn't move the baker forward.

rule.text: Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The setup compares the eyes looking to the LORD to bakers waiting on the oven for a batch. That points straight to food and rules out 'Rain for their fields' and 'Rest from their work' on card 12.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Both wrong answers start with 'Only' and the right answer starts with 'All', so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
